root_cause: Unsafe mission selectors flow through orchestrator-api read endpoints into the canonical read-path resolver, which correctly calls assert_safe_path_segment and raises ValueError for '..' or '../traversal'. The orchestrator-api mission resolver adapter handles StatusReadPathNotFound and normal absent-mission cases, but without translating ValueError at that shared boundary the exception escapes Typer command execution and is rendered as a raw traceback instead of the JSON-first error envelope required by the machine contract.
approach: Add a narrow ValueError catch in _resolve_mission_dir_or_fail, immediately alongside the existing StatusReadPathNotFound translation, and map it to _fail(command, "INVALID_MISSION", ...) with a data.message field containing the guard message. Keep the safe-path guard in the resolver unchanged so traversal remains fail-closed; only the orchestrator-api error presentation changes. Add a root-CLI regression test covering mission-state, list-ready, and resolve-workspace with unsafe --mission values, asserting stdout is parseable JSON with success=false, the specific orchestrator-api.<command> value, and error_code INVALID_MISSION.
tests_to_add: Parametrized regression in tests/agent/test_json_envelope_contract_integration.py for unsafe --mission selectors on mission-state, list-ready, and resolve-workspace through the root orchestrator-api command, asserting JSON envelope instead of traceback
risk_notes: Catching all ValueError at this boundary could accidentally classify an unrelated resolver ValueError as INVALID_MISSION, but the try block is scoped to mission directory resolution and the known source is the canonical path-segment guard.
out_of_scope_observations: Related human-facing command tracebacks such as next/research are covered by issue #2878 and should not be changed in this orchestrator-api machine-contract fix.
